Cardiovascular admissions place substantial pressure on the health system, not only through the number of events but through the time patients spend in hospital. Length of hospital stay (LOS) reflects severity, access to step-down care, and ward efficiency—all key considerations for service planning. We analysed median LOS (with 25th–75th percentiles) for eligible hospital-ascertained stroke and heart attack (acute myocardial infarction, AMI) admissions between 2010 and 2023, using routinely collected BNR data. Admissions ending in hospital death were included, and same-day stays counted as one hospital day. We summarised trends over time and used quantile (median) regression to explore differences by event type, sex, and two-year periods.
